title: Updating a field the role's Edit grant does not cover returns 200 and silently discards the value
statement: A role with an individual update grant scoped to a subset of fields does not refuse a write that names a field outside the grant. The ungranted value is stripped and the request answers 200 with the old value in the response body. The same product refuses at the action level with 403 No permissions when a role has no update grant at all, so refusal exists, just not per field.

handVerified.note: Report section 6. Reproduced exactly on a clean instance: role tcfldr with view on [id,alpha,beta] and update on [alpha] only; POST /api/tcfld:update {alpha:a1, beta:b1} answered 200 with beta:b0 and postgres kept 1|a1|b0. Two controls: sending only the ungranted field is a 200 no-op, and a role with no update grant gets 403. The report ADDS the mechanism cite, which findings.md carries none for.

source.howDecided: git log d8d8cb4b..origin/main -- <culprit files> returned 0 commits for every file in this finding. The only three commits since the tested SHA are 24a620efb8 and 032a4f6913 (lerna version bumps, packages/*/package.json and lerna.json only) and ba00bcebc2 (CHANGELOG.md, CHANGELOG.zh-CN.md). The culprit lines were then re-read at origin/main and match the report's quotes.

reevaluation: The finding stands unchanged. acl.ts has no commit between the tested SHA and today, and the beforeGrantAction hook is byte-identical at lines 120-131: for create and update it deletes ctx.params.fields and re-emits it as ctx.params.whitelist. A repository whitelist filters values on the way through and never rejects the request that carried extra keys, which is the whole defect. Nothing on the tracker touches it: the whole-repo sweep since 2026-08-19 found five unrelated items. Scope, severity and confidence are exactly as the report left them. This is the strongest finding in the batch: one hook, one mechanism, and the product's own 403 path proves it knows how to refuse.
notes: File the report's mechanism cite (acl.ts:120-131), not findings.md, which carries no cite for F13. Frame it as silent partial write, NOT as privilege escalation: the ungranted value is correctly not written, so nothing is leaked or over-written; the defect is that the caller is told the write succeeded. The response body itself is the proof (it returns beta:b0 while the request said b1), which makes a short reproduction possible without screenshots.
